concept.name: Component risk contribution
concept.definition: An asset's total contribution to portfolio risk, computed as its weight times its marginal risk contribution; component risk contributions sum exactly to total portfolio volatility by Euler's homogeneous-function theorem.
concept.intuition: It splits total portfolio risk into slices, one per asset, so you can see which positions actually eat your risk budget - often very different from which positions eat your capital.
concept.mechanics: CRC_i = w_i * MRC_i = w_i * (Cw)_i / sigma_p, and sum_i CRC_i = sigma_p. Expressed as percentages, CRC_i/sigma_p gives each asset's share of total risk, the quantity equalized in risk-parity (equal risk contribution) portfolios.
concept.formula: CRC_i = w_i * (Cw)_i / sigma_p, with sum_i CRC_i = sigma_p.
concept.failure_modes: Risk contributions depend on the chosen covariance estimate and risk measure, so they can be badly wrong in crises when correlations shift; negative contributions from hedging positions can also confuse naive budget checks.
concept.misconceptions: Dollar weights are not risk weights: a 60/40 stock/bond portfolio typically derives around 90% of its volatility from the equity sleeve, not 60%.
concept.example: In a 60/40 portfolio with 10% volatility, if the equity CRC is 9% and the bond CRC is 1%, equities consume 90% of the risk budget despite holding 60% of the capital.

citations.source: Thierry Roncalli, Introduction to Risk Parity and Budgeting
